chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

When you go out from your house for a journey or for staying at home, say: 'In the Name of Allah, I believe in Allah, I rely upon Allah, Whatever Allah so Desires, there is neither might nor strength except with Allah.' Then the devils will meet him and turn away, and the angels will strike their faces and say: 'What is your way to him? He has named Allah, believed in Him, relied upon Him, and said: Whatever Allah so Desires, there is neither might nor strength except with Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when leaving the house for protection from devils?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this supplication as a protective measure for the believer's transition from the private sphere to the public, emphasizing the spiritual mechanics of divine protection. The narration highlights the immediate reaction of the jinn and angels, illustrating how verbalizing trust (tawakkul) and God's will (mashi'a) effectively seals the believer against external spiritual influences. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating daily actions with conscious dhikr to maintain spiritual vigilance.
